title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
statement: Merge two sorted singly linked lists into one sorted list by splicing their nodes together, and return its head.

hints.1_question: Look at the heads of both lists. Which one belongs next in the merged list?
hints.2_nudge: Use a dummy head and a tail pointer. Repeatedly attach the smaller head to the tail. When one list runs out, attach the other whole.
hints.3_big_hint: while l1 and l2: attach the smaller, advance it and the tail. Finally cur.next = l1 or l2. Return dummy.next.

known_bugs.name: drops the leftover nodes of the longer list
known_bugs.followup: When one list runs out, what happens to the remaining nodes of the other?

known_bugs.name: crashes when a list is empty
known_bugs.followup: What is `l1.val` when l1 is None?

known_bugs.name: recursive merge (hits Python's recursion limit)
known_bugs.followup: How deep does the recursion go for two lists of 50000 nodes, and what limit does Python have?

followups: Why does a dummy node simplify the code?
How would the recursive version trade clarity for stack space?
